title: feat(sharing,ui): the In a queue toggle shows only on objects that use queues
body:
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBSd8RGmmLiVBikxTmsKRPnt)_ repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufziJJZ4CWE7fc4YEVnq Fixes #34602 ## 维护者速读 - **改了什么**：列表工具栏的「In a queue」开关只在真正用到队列的对象上出现：该对象现在有记录停在队列里，或有生效的分配规则把它的新记录派进队列。其余对象默认不显示。 - **为什么改**：以前只要组织有一个队列，所有带负责人的对象都显示这个开关，绝大多数对象点了只会得到空列表。按 2026-11-17 裁决，由服务端自动判断，不新增任何配置项。 - **风险与回滚**：`/auth/me/permissions` 多一个字段 `objectsUsingQueues`（只列调用者能读的对象名，不含队列名和数量）；组织有队列时每次会话多约 N+1 次 `limit 1` 读取。回滚即还原本 PR。 - **先看**：`packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts`（判断逻辑）和 `ui/packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`（开关门槛）。 - **两分钟验证**：在有队列的组织里打开一个从没进过队列的对象列表，开关不出现；把一条记录放进队列（清空负责人、设队列）后重新登录或刷新，开关出现。 - **需要你做的**：无需决定；#34623 已合并，本分支已合入 `origin/main`（合并提交 `43a9211d`），由席位审阅后落地。 ## What changes The "In a queue" toggle on a list now shows only on an object where a queue can hold something, as ruled on this card (comment 6937524209): - a record of the object sits in a queue now (no owner, a queue set), or - an active assignment rule routes the object's new records into a queue: one of the organization's own `sys_assignment_rule` rows, or a rule an installed package declares that the activation ledger has not switched off. Nothing is authored (ruling 6429748166 stands). Per the card's condition, the answer widens the response that already serves `hasAnyQueue` (#28508) rather than adding an endpoint: | Layer | Change | |---|---| | `packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts` | `MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponseSchema` (strict) gains the required sibling `objectsUsingQueues: string[]`. | | `packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts` | `IOwnershipQueueService` gains the optional `objectsUsingQueues?(organizationId)`. | | `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` | Implements it: the queue-column objects, plus the objects a routing rule names, then one `limit 1` sitting read per remaining object (8 at a time) in system context. A failed read is warned once and leaves that object out. | | `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` | `GET /auth/me/permissions` asks only when `hasAnyQueue` is true and narrows the list to objects the caller may read (`allowRead`). `[]` when the service or method is missing, throws, or answers a non-array, and on the closed body. | | `@object-ui/permissions` | `MePermissionsProvider` forwards the field; the context type carries it as optional (undefined = no answer). | | `@object-ui/plugin-list` | `queueFilterOffered` adds `objectUsesQueues(objectsUsingQueues, schema.objectName)` to the existing `hasAnyQueue === true && objectHasOwnershipQueue(def)` gate. | The spec surface was widened with the seat's approval (claim amendment 6937613028). This is the same single-PR shape as #28508. ## Why Before this change, a single queue in the organization put the toggle on every list of every object with a user owner. On most of them nothing ever sits in a queue, so the toggle could only return an empty list (#34602). ## Disclosure, against #28508's "Only the boolean" #28508 kept the answer to one boolean so that a member who may not read `sys_queue` learns nothing about queues beyond "there is one". This field adds the following: - **What it reveals:** per object, whether a queue can hold something on it (a record sits in a queue now, or a rule routes there). It does not reveal queue names, queue membership, counts, which rule routes, or which records sit. - **To whom:** only the signed-in caller, about objects they may already read. The route drops every name whose `objects[name].allowRead` is not `true`, so an object the caller cannot read never appears. This is pinned in the hono tests and through the real door in `packages/verify`, where an admin sees `qobj_secret` and a member does not. - **The degraded body** (permissions could not be resolved) carries the list unnarrowed, because there is no `objects` map to narrow by. It only ever names objects in the caller's own organization, and the UI already treats the degraded body as unknown. - **Nothing on the closed body:** the outer catch's body carries `[]`, and an anonymous caller is told only `{ authenticated: false }`. - **No environment-wide answer across a wall** (seat rulings on #34602, comments 6940335886 and 6941437476): a person outside every organization (`isOutsideEveryOrganization`) gets `[]`, and so does any caller with no active organization under `isolated` or `group`. In both cases the service is never asked with `null`. Under `single`, or with no `tenancy` service, a caller with no active organization keeps the environment-wide read. An unreadable posture answers `[]`. Pinned in the hono tests and ablated (commits `9a917959`, `18bca3ca`). ## Cost (measured) The measurement was a temporary `packages/verify` probe, deleted before commit. It used a real kernel, sqlite-wasm in memory, a declared queue and no rules. The dataset had 30 owned objects with 2,000 rows each, plus one object with 50,000 rows, all in one organization. This is the card's "HotCRM-sized" target, as an estimate: I did not count HotCRM's objects from this repo. | Reading | n | Median | p90 | Max | |---|---|---|---|---| | Reads per `objectsUsingQueues` call | — | **32** (1 `sys_assignment_rule` read + 1 sitting read per owned object) | | | | `objectsUsingQueues` alone, nothing sitting (worst case) | 20 | 11.02 ms | 12.63 ms | 13.02 ms | | `objectsUsingQueues` alone, a parked record in every object | 20 | 9.24 ms | 11.99 ms | 12.81 ms | | One sitting read on the 50,000-row object, no match | 10 | 0.62 ms | 0.84 ms | 0.84 ms | | Control: a no-match `limit 1` read on an unindexed text column of the same object | 10 | 5.04 ms | 7.97 ms | 7.97 ms | | `GET /auth/me/permissions` with the answer | 30 | 17.97 ms | 30.22 ms | 37.52 ms | | `GET /auth/me/permissions` without it (method shadowed) | 30 | 7.91 ms | 9.37 ms | 9.99 ms | A first run on the same rig gave 13.04 / 21.92 / 7.93 ms medians for the three main readings. These are shared-box timings, not idle-box figures. - The added cost is about 10 ms per permissions read for 30 objects. It is paid only when the organization has a queue (`hasAnyQueue` true), and only once per session, because the console reads this payload once. - There is no index on the `queue` column. On a server database, the worst case per object is a scan of the organization's rows of that object when nothing sits in a queue. The 50,000-row reading above stays under 1 ms on sqlite, and the control read is slower than it. If a very large tenant shows up in profiling, an index on `(organization_id, queue)` is the follow-up. This PR does not add one. ## Staleness (measured by reading the code path, pinned in tests) `MePermissionsProvider` refetches only when its `requestKey` changes (a sign-in, sign-out or organization switch) or the page reloads. So: - A record that starts sitting in a queue on an object that is not listed yet shows the toggle from the **next sign-in, organization switch or reload**. Until then the toggle stays hidden on that object. - The reverse direction behaves the same way: the last queued record leaving keeps the toggle until the next read. - A new routing rule shows from the next read too. The docs paragraph in `content/docs/automation/queues-and-assignment-rules.mdx` says this to authors. ## Verification Clause-②: yes (widening) Metadata-protocol: added Skills-docs: none — a served /auth/me/permissions answer read by the console; no skill under skills/** or ui/skills/** teaches that route (grep hasAnyQueue / me/permissions on main: 0 hits)
Before / after readings **Behaviour (the card's scenario):** the organization has one queue, and object `B` has a user owner but nothing ever sits in a queue on it. - Before: `B`'s list shows "In a queue", and turning it on returns an empty list. - After: `B`'s list shows no toggle. An object with a record sitting in a queue, or one a rule routes into a queue, still shows it. **Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: each mutation landed, was measured, and was restored to `git diff HEAD` empty): | Mutation | Test | Reading | |---|---|---| | `ListView.tsx`: `&& objectUsesQueues(objectsUsingQueues, schema.objectName)` → `&& true` (the pre-#34602 gate) | `ListView.queueSittingFilter-25769.test.tsx` | 2 failed / 18 passed: "the organization has a queue but this object is not named: no toggle…" and "an answer without the list … hides the toggle". Restored: 20/20. | | `current-user-endpoints.ts`: drop the `readableObjectsUsingQueues(…)` narrowing | `current-user-endpoints-has-any-queue.test.ts` | 1 failed / 15 passed: "the service's answer … is carried, minus the objects the caller may not read". Restored: 16/16. | | `ownership-queue-service.ts`: the sitting read always answers `false` | `ownership-queue.test.ts` | 4 failed / 75 passed (no-rule, sitting-record, union, failed-read cases). Restored: 79/79. |
Tests and type-checks (all under scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh) | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `@objectstack/spec` `api/me-permissions-response.test.ts` + authorable surface | 2 files, 15 tests, exit 0 | | `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` `ownership-queue.test.ts` (12 new) | 79 tests, exit 0 | | `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` (has-any-queue, envelope, outer-catch) | 3 files, 32 tests, exit 0 | | `@objectstack/client` `auth-me-permissions.test.ts` | 3 tests, exit 0 | | `@objectstack/verify` `me-permissions-has-any-queue.test.ts` (4 new, real door) | 9 tests, exit 0 | | `ui` queueSittingFilter-25769, emptyStateClearFilters-28908, hasAnyQueue-28428 | 3 files, 34 tests, exit 0 | | `typecheck`: spec, plugin-sharing, plugin-hono-server, client, verify | exit 0 | | `type-check`: @object-ui/permissions, @object-ui/plugin-list | exit 0 | | `type-check`: app-shell, plugin-detail, plugin-form, plugin-grid, plugin-view, plugin-kanban, plugin-calendar, plugin-gantt, fields, plugin-report, console (every UI package whose fixtures changed) | 11 × exit 0 | | The 13 app-shell tests + the verify door test edited for `check:test-source-alias` | 13 files, 77 tests + 9 tests, exit 0 | | `eslint` on the changed files (root config for `packages/**`, `ui/` config for `ui/**`) | exit 0, 0 errors |
Derived gates `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived **125** commands on head `a342f155`. All 125 ran serially on that head, each `:: exit 0`. `dispatch-gates --ran` reported: 125 derived, 125 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN (exit 0). On the first pass, over the previous head: - 4 gates exited 3 on prerequisites, and nothing was measured. `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` needed its pinned fixture commit fetched. `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` needed a `packages/**` build. - 1 gate found a real problem. `check:test-source-alias` flagged 14 edited test files whose first dynamic-import load fell inside a clocked case. Fixed in `a342f155` with module-top side-effect imports, the same shape as the existing precedents. Re-run in full on the merged head `b92c81f1`: 125 derived, 125 × exit 0, `--ran` clean. The delta after it (`18bca3ca`, route + schema text) re-ran `check:test-source-alias`, `check:undeclared-dep-imports`, spec `check:generated`, eslint and the hono/spec/verify suites, all exit 0. `spec check:generated` named `content/docs/references/**` as stale. It was regenerated with `gen:docs` and committed (`ceb31f71`).
## Acceptance notes - Lands after #34580 (PR #34623 touches the same chip in `ListView.tsx`). #34623 has merged, and this branch merged `origin/main` in `43a9211d` (the ListView conflict keeps all four conditions plus #34580's reset effect) and re-ran the list, harness and permissions tests (132/132). - About 140 UI test fixtures gained `objectsUsingQueues: []` next to `hasAnyQueue`, because the spec response type now requires the field. One fixture (`ListView.emptyStateClearFilters-28908`) carries `[OBJECT]` because it exercises the toggle. These are mechanical, with no behaviour change. - The L2 contract review is owed by seat 3. Fix rounds after it: S1 (`725327700`, an object without a tenant column is not filtered on that column), M1 (`3565460bd`, the read always carries the caller's tenantId), S2 (migration paragraph in the changeset), S3 and the walled no-active-organization rule (`9a917959e`, `18bca3ca6`). Each round has a pin and an ablation. - N4 (accepted deviation, contract review 6940335886): a tenancy-disabled object that declares its own organization_id gets the explicit organization predicate, so a parked row with an empty or other organization_id is not counted and the toggle can stay hidden on such an object; it fails in the hidden direction and no object in this tree has the shape. ## Human Minimum - [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. - [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind. - [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes. - [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request. - [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset. - [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed. - [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`. - [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English. - [x] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01WGufziJJZ4CWE7fc4YEVnq
